open_points.subject: RegistryFailureKind transport failure member naming
open_points.text: _registry_url: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST join only the supplied relative path to the deployment URL loaded from the environment variable the imported REGISTRY_BASE_URL_VARIABLE constant names, preserving that URL's own path prefix so a Registry deployed under a prefix keeps it on every request. Each of the following MUST raise RegistryBoundaryError carrying the TRANSPORT_ERROR member of = models.RegistryFailureKind, never a raw KeyError, ValueError, or other untyped error, and never a repaired URL: the variable is absent or empty; its value is not a usable http or https base URL; its value carries userinfo credentials, which are rejected rather than stripped, retained, or forwarded; the supplied path is absolute or protocol-relative, which MUST NOT be allowed to replace the host or scheme.
open_points.other_text: _translate_registry_failure: [BEHAVIOR] MUST translate each closed failure into its member of = models.RegistryFailureKind, so an invalid identifier gives its invalid_uuid member, an unknown project its not_found member, an inactive project its archived member, a timeout its timeout member, a transport failure its transport_error member, a non-success HTTP status its http_error member, an invalid body its schema_mismatch member and a response for another project its identity_mismatch member, and MUST NOT fall back to cached, client-supplied, or fabricated context.
open_points.question: Must the transport-failure enum member be named TRANSPORT_ERROR, as the changed requirement and runtime enum surface state, or transport_error, as _translate_registry_failure states?
